$comment: Shared cloud read-aloud contract. Input sentences are the texts the read-aloud pipeline speaks after speakable-text (placeholders already localized). bodyCases reference entries {providerKind, direction, model} in the data object of shared/model-contracts/voice_catalog_contract.v2.json.

chunks: Lengths are Unicode scalar counts (not grapheme clusters, not UTF-16). Trim sentences (whitespace set of dictation.v1.json) and drop empty ones. Chunk 1 = sentence 1, plus sentence 2 when "s1 s2" fits in min(200, maxChars) code points.

Chunk k (k >= 2) packs whole sentences joined by one space up to limit_k = min(maxChars, 1000, 200 × 2^(k−1)) code points (400, 800, 1000, 1000, …). A sentence is never split (speakable-text caps sentences at 200).
Requests are serial; while chunk k plays only chunk k+1 is fetched. Stopping cancels the in-flight request.
readingLanguage: Take the hypothesis with the highest confidence (ties: the lexicographically smallest tag, since iOS hypotheses are an unordered dictionary); if there is none or its confidence < 0.5, use the app UI locale. Detector tags are kept as given (BCP-47).
xaiLanguage: Normalise first (_ → -, in / iw / ji → id / he / yi). Case-insensitive exact match in xaiTtsLanguages → that spelling; else the primary subtag when it is in the list (zh-Hans / zh-Hant → zh); else xaiDefaultRegion for the primary subtag; else auto.
body: openai_speech: {model, input, voice, response_format = entry.outputFormat, speed?}. xai_tts: {text, voice_id, language, output_format: {codec: entry.outputFormat}, speed?} — no model field (catalog id xai-tts is ours).

Effective speed: compute in double precision (Android converts the Float slider value to Double first); clamp the slider value to the catalog entry speedRange {min, max}, then round half up to 2 decimals as floor(x × 100 + 0.5) / 100 (not banker's rounding, not toFixed); omit speed when the result equals 1. An entry without speedRange does not support speed (e.g. groq Orpheus): the effective speed is 1 and speed is never sent. A missing slider value = 1. The cache key field speed is this effective speed, not the raw slider value.
Key order in expected is the canonical order; JSON key order is not significant on the wire.

Cases with input.apiKey carry expected.headers: auth header by transport only (gemini_* → x-goog-api-key: <key>; others → Authorization: Bearer <key>) plus Content-Type: application/json. gemini_tts: {model, store: false, input: [{type: user_input, content: [{type: text, text}]}], response_format: {type: audio, mime_type: audio/wav}, generation_config: {speech_config: [{voice}]}}. mistral_speech: {model, input, voice_id, response_format: mp3}. dashscope_tts: {model, input: {text, voice, language_type}}; language_type maps the normalised primary subtag of the reading language zh→Chinese en→English de→German it→Italian pt→Portuguese es→Spanish ja→Japanese ko→Korean fr→French ru→Russian, anything else Auto. The new TTS transports never send speed.
failure: Per chunk, auto retry follows dictation failure rules. When not retrying (including 401 / 403), continue from the failed chunk with the system engine and show the fallback notice once.
audioResponse: expected = {audioBase64} (decode it: these bytes are the audio, cached and played; not the JSON) | {downloadUrl} (GET it without auth headers; non-2xx follows the same status rules; the body bytes are the wav audio) | null (invalid response: no retry, fall back to the system engine as today).

gemini_tts: data of the first steps[].content[] item with type == audio. mistral_speech: top-level audio_data. dashscope_tts: output.audio.url, must be https. Missing field, bad base64 (standard alphabet, padded) or empty decoded audio → null.
reviewUnification: Review unification (X-VPRIV): base64 must be strict (length multiple of 4, padded, standard alphabet) or the response is invalid; the dashscope download URL is parsed as a URL, scheme compared case-insensitively to https and host must be non-empty; gemini_tts takes only the first audio block and an empty data there is invalid (no searching further); dashscope_tts only accepts output.audio.url, data without url is invalid; JSON requests send only the auth header and Content-Type (no Accept); mistral_speech always sends response_format mp3; JSON and base64 decoding stays off the main thread.

Accept: code never sets Accept explicitly; Accept headers added by the HTTP stack or a client plugin do not count, and expected.headers compares only explicitly set headers. Download URL host: any non-empty host a lenient URL parser accepts (underscores allowed); URL-safe base64 alphabet (- _) is invalid.
